description: Move one or more assets to one or more locations: record a movement, the event that changes where an asset is.

discriminating_flow.title: A pending movement does not change where the asset is; the done one before it still stands

probe_semantics: Record a movement event referencing the assets moved and the locations they are moved to, at a stated lifecycle status and effective time, so that a later read of an asset's current location reflects it.

provenance.why: The flow DSL had no location verbs, so the ten asset-location-movement fixtures the kernel cites carry provenance:null and were never observed (MetaCoding-4vh). Without `move` there is no way to reach the state a location read is about.

description: Whether an asset is currently at a given location.

discriminating_flow.title: The latest done movement decides where the asset is; the earlier location is left

probe_semantics: Deliver whether a given location asset is among the locations the source currently reports for the subject asset, so an assertion can confirm where a thing is against an expected place.

provenance.why: The core location read. Unblocks the OBSERVE half of MetaCoding-4vh, whose ten location fixtures are synthetic.

description: How many locations an asset is currently reported to be at.

discriminating_flow.title: A movement to two locations puts the asset at both, where a later single move leaves one

probe_semantics: Deliver the number of locations the source currently reports for the subject asset, so an assertion can tell being in one place from being in several and from being nowhere.

provenance.why: Distinguishes 'moved away' from 'moved additionally': a port that appends locations instead of replacing them reads the same on is_at_location for the new place and differs only here.

description: The shape on the ground an asset currently occupies, as the source reports it.

discriminating_flow.title: A movable asset's shape on the ground comes from its own movement, not from the place it was moved to

probe_semantics: Deliver the geometry the source currently reports for the subject asset as a single well-known-text string, so an assertion can confirm where on the ground a thing is; the empty string when the source reports none.

provenance.why: One of the three kernel location rows src/kernel/status.ts labels observed and is not (MetaCoding-4vh): 'a non-fixed asset's geometry comes from its confirmed movement'.

description: Whether an asset may hold other assets — whether it is a place things can be at.

discriminating_flow.title: A field is a place things can be at; an animal is not

probe_semantics: Deliver whether the source marks the subject asset as one that other assets can be located at, so an assertion can tell a place from a thing.

provenance.why: The flag the location surface is gated on; observed so the per-entity DEFAULT (a field is a place, an animal is not) is a recorded fact rather than an assumption.

description: Whether an asset stays put — whether it has a shape of its own rather than one it acquires by being moved.

discriminating_flow.title: A fixed asset keeps its own shape and is placed nowhere, however it is moved

probe_semantics: Deliver whether the source marks the subject asset as one that does not move, so an assertion can tell an asset whose shape comes from itself from one whose shape comes from its movements.

provenance.why: The contrast the geometry kernel row needs: a fixed asset ignores movements entirely (validated live 2026-07-28: locations empty, geometry its own).

description: Whether an asset was at a given location at a stated moment — the as-of read, distinct from where it is now.

discriminating_flow.title: An asset that moved on in June was still in the earlier field in March

probe_semantics: Deliver whether a given location was among the asset's locations as of a stated instant, so an assertion can ask where a thing WAS rather than only where it is.

provenance.why: The 'no explicit as-of read' gap (wave1-readiness-2026-07-20 §2). farmOS offers NO as-of read at its boundary — the asset's location relationship is computed at now (validated live 2026-07-28) — so this is a fold of OURS over the movement logs, a separate term from is_at_location because one ProbeSpec carries one authority.

description: How many assets are at a location — the question asked from the place's side rather than the thing's.

discriminating_flow.title: Two of three animals moved to the paddock: the paddock holds two and the other field none

probe_semantics: Deliver how many assets the source reports at the subject location as of a stated instant (or now when none is stated), so an assertion can ask what is in a place rather than asking each thing where it is.

punts: counts assets the source publishes at the location, including any a flow did not create — a shared oracle makes this a real hazard, so flows scope it with a location no other flow uses
provenance.why: The 'multi-asset fan-out' gap: one question ranging over many subjects, which is the question a farmer actually asks of a place. farmOS answers it internally only through a raw SQL query (filter[location.id] 500s, validated live 2026-07-28), so the fold is ours — over the asset bundles the source's OWN /api index publishes, of each asset's source-computed location. The membership stays farmOS's; only the enumeration is ours.

description: Whether an animal is recorded as unable to breed.

discriminating_flow.title: Recorded sterile, recorded fertile, and never said are three different answers

probe_semantics: Deliver whether the source records the subject animal as sterile, so an assertion can tell a recorded sterility from a recorded fertility and both from an unrecorded one.

provenance.why: The 'no sterility' gap (wave1-readiness-2026-07-20 §2). A real tri-state at the boundary — validated live 2026-07-28: unstated delivers null, true delivers true, false delivers false — so a port that treats absent as false is wrong in a way only this term can see.

description: The kind of animal an animal is recorded as — its breed or species grouping.

discriminating_flow.title: The kind an animal was created as is the kind the source reports

probe_semantics: Deliver the name of the animal kind the source records for the subject animal, so an assertion can confirm what sort of creature it is; the empty string when the source records none.

provenance.why: The 'no animal-type read-back' gap. The descriptor was writeable and unreadable, so every animal fixture stated a kind no assertion could confirm — a whole input with no observable.

description: The magnitude of one specific recorded measurement, addressed as itself rather than through the record that carries it.

discriminating_flow.title: Two weights on one harvest are two measurements, where the log reports only their sum

probe_semantics: Deliver the numeric magnitude the source records for the subject quantity, so an assertion can name ONE measurement where a read through its log would sum every measurement sharing a measure and unit.

provenance.why: The 'no quantity-level reads' gap. quantity_recorded sums every quantity on a log sharing a measure and unit — validated live 2026-07-28: 3 and 7 read back as 10.0 — so two measurements were one number and no fixture could tell a port that lost one from a port that kept both.

description: The role a recorded measurement plays — what the number is a measurement OF.

discriminating_flow.title: Two weights of the same unit are told apart by what each is a measurement of

probe_semantics: Deliver the label the source records for the subject quantity, so an assertion can tell two measurements of the same measure and unit apart by what each one is for; the empty string when the source records none.

provenance.why: The partner of quantity_measured_value: the value says how much, the label says of what. Without it a port could hold both magnitudes and have lost which is which.
